questions.questionText: What is the exact wording of Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?
options: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
No citizen shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to due process of law.
Every person has the right to life and liberty, subject to reasonable restrictions.
The State may deprive any person of life or liberty only in accordance with the Constitution.
questions.correctAnswer: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
questions.explanation: Article 21 contains a single sentence with that exact phrasing.

questions.questionText: Why did the drafters of the Indian Constitution avoid using the phrase "due process of law"?
options: They wanted to adopt language from the Japanese Constitution of 1946.
They believed "due process" gave too much power to the judiciary, as seen in the US Lochner era.
They thought "due process" was too vague for Indian legislation.
All of the above.
questions.explanation: The framers were influenced by Japanese wording, feared US-style judicial overreach, and found "due process" vague.

questions.questionText: Which constitutional advisor consulted with Justice Felix Frankfurter, leading to the adoption of "procedure established by law"?
options: M.N. Roy
Sir B.N. Rau
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
K.M. Munshi
questions.explanation: Sir B.N. Rau traveled to the US and discussed the due‑process issue with Justice Frankfurter.

questions.questionText: In A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras, how did the Supreme Court interpret "procedure established by law"?
options: As any legislative procedure, regardless of fairness
As a procedure that must be fair, reasonable, and just
As a procedure subject to judicial review for substantive justice
As a procedure limited to criminal cases only
questions.correctAnswer: As any legislative procedure, regardless of fairness
questions.explanation: The Court took a literal view: any law passed by Parliament satisfied the clause, even if unjust.

questions.questionText: What does the "Silo Theory" (doctrine of mutual exclusivity) assert about Fundamental Rights?
options: All Fundamental Rights are interdependent and form a single continuum
Each Fundamental Right operates in a separate, non‑overlapping compartment
Fundamental Rights can be suspended during emergencies
Article 21 overrides all other rights
questions.correctAnswer: Each Fundamental Right operates in a separate, non‑overlapping compartment
questions.explanation: Gopalan held that rights like Article 19 and Article 21 are distinct silos that cannot be cross‑invoked.

questions.questionText: Which Supreme Court case overturned the Gopalan doctrine and introduced a broader interpretation of Article 21?
options: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.correctAnswer: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
questions.explanation: The 1978 Maneka Gandhi judgment rejected the literalist view and linked Article 21 with fairness and natural justice.

questions.questionText: What is the "Golden Triangle" as articulated by Justice P.N. Bhagwati?
options: The relationship between Articles 14, 19 and 21
The three stages of judicial review: validity, reasonableness, and proportionality
The three pillars of Indian democracy: Legislature, Executive, Judiciary
The three rights: right to life, right to equality, right to freedom
questions.explanation: Justice Bhagwati described an organic connection among these three Articles, forming the Golden Triangle.

questions.questionText: In Maneka Gandhi's case, which specific freedom was held to be part of "personal liberty" under Article 21?
options: Freedom of speech
Freedom of movement within India
Right to travel abroad
Freedom of religion
questions.explanation: The Court recognized the right to travel abroad as an essential component of personal liberty.

questions.questionText: Which landmark judgment later recognized the fundamental right to privacy as part of Article 21?
options: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
Puttaswamy v. Union of India
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court in Puttaswamy (2017) declared privacy a fundamental right under Article 21.

questions.questionText: According to the lecture, what limits the scope of Article 21?
options: The existence of a valid statutory law with a fair, non‑arbitrary procedure
The discretion of the President alone
The absence of any legislative provision
The exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.correctAnswer: The existence of a valid statutory law with a fair, non‑arbitrary procedure
questions.explanation: Article 21 does not grant absolute immunity; it allows regulation when law is fair, non‑arbitrary, and serves legitimate state interests.
